title: intent cards follow ASD-STE100: one checker in bin/lib/fm_ste.py, new optional intent fields in the decision details, and fm-decide refuses an intent card whose English or Chinese text breaks the rules
acceptance: Why. The captain asked (2026-10-05) for the intent alignment card to use ASD-STE100 (Simplified Technical English) and approved the prototype published as the 'Intent Card Prototype' artifact (source ~/Desktop/firstmate-ops/prototypes/intent-card-ste/index.html, outside the repository; its rules are restated in full below so the worker never needs that file). Today every card's text is free prose with no writing standard and no check: firstmate's own cards that day had 60+ word single-sentence explanations, and nothing on a card restates the captain's goal, the scope, what 'done' means, or asks the captain to confirm any of it. The decision-details contract (design/design.md §5.2, the paragraph 'New requests require `--details <file>`', about :358-366) has only title, explanation, before, after, outcome and options A/B/C, validated by the jq block in bin/fm-decide.sh (about :372-390). This task adds the checker, the optional intent fields and their validation at request time. Rendering on the board and in fm-diagram.sh, and recording the captain's answers to confirm questions, are T-211 (depends on this task). The captain did not answer the five open questions on the prototype; this spec uses these defaults, each changeable later by a card: (1) STE is enforced when an intent card is raised; (2) a 'No, change it' answer turns the answer into a spec-change request (T-211); (3) the Chinese rules Z1-Z8 and glossary below; (4) cards only, PR bodies and worker briefs are out of scope; (5) no light theme.

One checker, in one module: new bin/lib/fm_ste.py (Python 3.9-compatible, standard library only, no network). It exposes (a) `check(text, kind=None) -> {lang, n, max, kind, issues:[{rule, detail, severity}]}` for one sentence, where kind is 'step' (an instruction) or 'fact' (a description) and None means auto-detect (an English sentence is a step when its first word is in IMPERATIVE; a Chinese one when it matches ZH_IMPERATIVE); (b) `split(text) -> [sentences]`, splitting English after `.`, `!` or `?` followed by whitespace and Chinese after `。`, `！` or `？`, dropping empty pieces; (c) `label(text) -> same shape` for a diagram node label; (d) `check_details(details) -> report` described below; (e) a CLI: `python3 bin/lib/fm_ste.py check-details <file>` prints the report as JSON and exits 0 when the details are an intent card that passes, 65 when an intent card fails (report printed, every failing sentence listed on stderr as `<lang> <field>: <sentence> -> <rule> <detail>`), 64 when the new fields are malformed, and 0 with `{"intent_card": false}` for details carrying none of the new fields; `python3 bin/lib/fm_ste.py rules` prints the rule table as JSON (ids, text en and zh-TW, limits, word lists) so T-211's board shows the same rules from generated data and never a second copy. No other file may define these rules or word lists.

English rules (ASD-STE100 subset a script can check), each with its id and severity. A sentence fails when it has any 'fail' issue; 'warn' issues are reported but never fail. R1 a step has at most 20 words (fail). R2 a fact has at most 25 words (fail). Words are runs matching `[A-Za-z0-9#][A-Za-z0-9#'._/-]*`. R3 one instruction per step: a step fails when a second IMPERATIVE verb follows `,`, `;`, `and`, `then` or `and then` (regex `(,|;|\band then\b|\bthen\b|\band\b)\s+(<IMPERATIVE>)\b`, case-insensitive) (fail). R4 active voice: PASSIVE = `\b(is|are|was|were|be|been|being|gets|got)\s+(\w+ly\s+)?(\w+ed|built|done|found|given|held|kept|known|made|met|paid|put|read|run|seen|sent|set|shown|split|taken|told|written|thrown|broken|chosen)\b` (case-insensitive) is fail in a step and warn in a fact. R5 no modal: `\b(will|would|could|should|shall|might)\b` (fail). R6 approved words: UNAPPROVED maps utilize->use, utilise->use, ensure->make sure, perform->do, approximately->about, commence->start, terminate->stop, 'prior to'->before, 'in order to'->to, via->through, obtain->get, additional->more, require->need, requires->needs, 'is able to'->can, 'are able to'->can, facilitate->help, subsequently->then, numerous->many, regarding->about, attempt->try, sufficient->enough, indicate->show, indicates->shows, modify->change, initiate->start, assist->help; each match is case-insensitive on word boundaries (multi-word entries match any whitespace between words) and is fail with detail `<found> -> <use>`. R7 -ing words: a word longer than 4 letters ending in 'ing', all lowercase after its first letter, not in ING_OK = {string, thing, during, nothing, something, anything, everything, ring, bring, king, spring, sting, swing, ping, pending, missing, existing, following, remaining, timing, timings, sharding, routing, ceiling, pricing, preflight, warning, morning, evening, building} (warn). R8 no vague words or contractions: VAGUE = `\b(etc\.?|and/or|some|appropriate|appropriately|properly|various|relevant)\b`, CONTRACTION = `\b\w+'(t|s|re|ve|ll|d)\b`, both case-insensitive (fail). R9 a note inside a step: a step matching `\b(note|caution|warning|important)\b[:\s]` (case-insensitive) (fail). IMPERATIVE = add allow approve ask change check choose close confirm copy delete dispatch do find fix give hold keep let make merge move open put read record remove repin replace rerun run send set show start stop tell type update use wait widen write. R10 (at most 6 sentences per paragraph, at most 3 nouns in a cluster) is documented in the rule table as 'checked by eye' and never computed.

Chinese rules (STE has no Chinese standard; this is the captain-approved equivalent). Length counts each CJK ideograph (U+4E00-U+9FFF) as one and each Latin run matching `[A-Za-z0-9#._/-]+` as one. Z1 a step has at most 25 units, a fact at most 30 (fail). Z2 one action per step: ZH_MULTI = `(並且|並|然後|再|同時|以及|接著)` in a step (fail). Z3 no passive: ZH_PASSIVE = `(被|受到|由[^，。]{1,8}所)` (fail). Z4 no future or modal: ZH_MODAL = `(將會|將|應該|應當|會不會)` (fail). Z5 no vague words: ZH_VAGUE = `(可能|大概|左右|等等|適當|盡量|相關|一些|之類)` (fail). Z6 one term per meaning, glossary {併入->合併, 審核->審查, 分派->派工, 檢閱->審查, 佈署->部署, 預審->預檢} (fail, detail `<found> -> <use>`). Z7 a note inside a step: a step matching `(注意|警告)[：:]` (fail). Z8 (at most 6 sentences per paragraph) is documented and never computed. ZH_IMPERATIVE = `^(請)?(合併|派工|派|審查|重跑|重新|修|修正|移除|加入|改|更新|確認|停|停止|啟動|寫|讀|搬|搬到|放|保留|檢查|執行|跑|選|設|設定|擴大|發|等)`. A sentence is Chinese when it contains any CJK ideograph. Technical names (paths, ids, flags, code in backticks) count as one unit or word each and are never checked for vocabulary: text inside backticks is replaced by a single placeholder word before any rule runs.

Labels. A diagram node label (T-211 draws them) is checked as a fact with a tighter length: at most 6 English words or 14 Chinese units (rule id R2 or Z1 with detail `<n> > <max>`), plus every other fail rule above. A label is not split into sentences.

The new optional decision-details fields, per locale (`en` and `zh-TW`, each optional field present in both or in neither): `intent` (array of {kind: 'step'|'fact', text}), `why` (same), `scope_in` and `scope_out` (arrays of strings, each 1-200 code points, plain labels, not checked as sentences), `done` (array of {kind, text}), `notes` (array of {kind: 'note'|'caution', text}, text checked as facts, split into sentences), `questions` (array of {kind, text}, 1-6 items, the same count in both locales), `before_nodes` and `after_nodes` (arrays of {state: 'same'|'gone'|'new', label}, 1-8 items each; 'gone' only in before_nodes, 'new' only in after_nodes; the same counts in both locales), and `change_table` (array of {text, A, B, C} where A/B/C are each one of '✓', '—', '?', 1-8 rows, the same count in both locales). Every text is a string, 1-2000 code points, with the same prohibited-control rule fm-decide already applies (C0 except tab/LF/CR, DEL, C1, lone surrogates). Arrays of {kind,text} hold 1-12 items. A details object carrying `intent` in a locale is an intent card; `intent` is required in both locales when any new field is present (otherwise exit 64). Unknown keys inside a locale are left alone (forward compatible); the existing required fields are unchanged.

What is checked on an intent card, per locale: title (as one fact, not split), explanation, before, after and outcome (each split into sentences, auto kind), every option's description (as one step when it starts with an IMPERATIVE word / ZH_IMPERATIVE, else a fact, not split), pros and cons (split, facts), every intent/why/done/questions item (split, with the item's kind applied to each piece), notes (split, facts), and every before_nodes/after_nodes label (label rules). The report is `{intent_card: true, ok: bool, locales: {en: [...], "zh-TW": [...]}, labels: {en: [...], "zh-TW": [...]}}` where each entry is {field, index (or null), sentence, kind, n, max, issues}. A card without the new fields is never checked (default 4: no change for cards raised by scripts, e.g. `fm.sh self-update` at bin/fm.sh:690-716, which builds its zh-TW from proposal text).

fm-decide.sh: in the strict --details path (bin/fm-decide.sh, after the existing locale jq check about :372-390 and the effect check about :395-405, before `pr_agrees`/binding and before any pending write), when the details file has any of the new keys in either locale, run `python3 "$HERE/lib/fm_ste.py" check-details "$DETAILS"` (refuse with exit 70 and a clear message if bin/lib/fm_ste.py is missing). Exit 64 from it -> fm-decide exits 64 with its message; exit 65 -> fm-decide exits 65, prints `fm-decide: the card's text breaks the STE rules; nothing was written` followed by the checker's per-sentence lines, and writes no pending record. On success the report is stored in the pending record as `ste` (next to `details`), so the board (T-211) displays the check read-only without recomputing it. When the details carry none of the new fields, fm-decide behaves exactly as today and never runs the checker (so fixtures that copy fm-decide.sh without bin/lib keep working). The legacy title-only skill path is unchanged.

Firstmate writes intent cards. skills/firstmate/SKILL.md, section `## Author and verify captain decisions` (about :702-760): extend the `--details` JSON example (about :708-738) with the optional intent fields, and update the prose copy of the validator's field list (about :740-747, 'The actual jq validator requires…') to name the optional fields, the `python3 bin/lib/fm_ste.py check-details <file>` step and fm-decide's exits 64 (malformed new fields) and 65 (STE refusal). Add the rule: every dispatch card, merge card and scope-widening card firstmate raises carries the intent fields (intent, why, scope_in, scope_out, done, notes when there is a caution, questions for anything firstmate is unsure of, before_nodes/after_nodes) and passes check-details before `--request`; a refusal is fixed by rewriting the text, never by dropping the intent fields. Keep the wording in that file's own style.

Tests. New tests/ste.test.sh (sourcing tests/lib.sh, assertions only from tests/lib.sh's set; any Python it runs lives in a new tests/lib/ste_cases.py, not in a heredoc) covering: every English rule R1-R9 with one failing and one passing sentence each, including R4 fail in a step and warn in a fact and R7 as warn; every Chinese rule Z1-Z7 likewise; backtick spans counted as one word and exempt from vocabulary rules; split() on English, Chinese and mixed text; label limits (6 words / 14 units); check-details exit codes 0/65/64 and the `{intent_card:false}` output for legacy details; the `rules` command's JSON containing every rule id R1-R10 and Z1-Z8 with en and zh-TW text. Real text fixtures (these exact strings; the worker needs nothing outside the repository): passing with kind=None — 'Move the coverage program into bin/lib/fm_ci_checks.py.' (step), 'Keep each message and each exit code the same.' (step), 'The coverage check in T-196 is correct.' (fact), 'The sandbox stops the save, and cursor waits 30 to 40 seconds.' (fact), '把覆蓋率程式搬到 bin/lib/fm_ci_checks.py。' (fact under auto-detection, since 把 is not in ZH_IMPERATIVE), '保留每一則訊息和每一個退出碼。' (step), 'T-196 的覆蓋率檢查是對的。' (fact), '沙盒擋下這次寫入，cursor 卡住 30 到 40 秒。' (fact). Failing samples, each checked with kind='step' and asserted to report at least the listed rules: 'Ensure the reviewer is notified, and then merge the PR after CI passes, etc.' -> at least R6 (Ensure -> make sure), R4 (is notified), R3 (then merge), R8 (etc.); '請確認 reviewer 被通知，然後在 CI 通過後併入 PR，大概十分鐘左右。' -> at least Z2 (然後), Z3 (被), Z5 (大概, 左右), Z6 (併入 -> 合併). In tests/decide.test.sh (1053 lines now; stay under 1200, or put the new cases in tests/ste.test.sh using the same fixture pattern): an intent card that passes is written with an `ste` report; one failing sentence refuses with exit 65, lists the sentence and rule, and writes no pending file; malformed new fields exit 64 (missing intent with other new fields, mismatched question counts, 'new' in before_nodes); details without new fields are accepted exactly as today and the record has no `ste` key.

Docs, edited in place (T-189): design/design.md §5.2 'Captain decisions', the paragraph 'New requests require `--details <file>`' (about :358-366): add the optional intent fields, the STE check at request time, the `ste` report on the pending record and the pointer to bin/lib/fm_ste.py; and §8 'The captain's board', subsection 'Interaction' (about :2147), one paragraph that T-211 renders the intent sections. Name the five defaults and that each is changeable by a card.

In flight. Cards already pending when this lands have no new fields and are untouched; the board renders them exactly as today. No stored record changes shape except new intent cards gaining `ste`. No other open task edits bin/fm-decide.sh or adds bin/lib/fm_ste.py; T-211 depends on this task and starts after it merges.

Workers do not run the suites. Evidence is the required GitHub check and the six gates. Fail-first is expected from tests/ste.test.sh (all red on base, where bin/lib/fm_ste.py does not exist) and the new decide cases (red on base, where intent fields are not checked); the legacy-details cases are regression guards, green on base and head. No vendor stub is involved.
